items.caption: NRG Dashboard automatically detects all installed NRG-Stack partner modules (InverterHub, MeterHub, ChargerHub, HeishaMon, Tessie) through their contracts - no manual linking of variable IDs needed.
Manual data points and the consumer list complement the automatic search, they do not replace it - both work at the same time.

items.name: HookInfo
items.caption: IPSView/popup: the tile also runs as a standalone web page at http://<Symcon-IP>:3777%s (auto-refresh every 30 s). In IPSView, place a WebView element on a popup page and enter this URL. Note: WebHooks can be reached on the local network without logging in.

Demo mode (01.09.2026): an instance of its own with this box ticked still shows all devices/values, but hides every wallbox control (enable/limit/start/stop) completely - neither does the frontend show switches, nor does the WebHook accept control commands. Intended for demo/showcase instances that must have no effect on real devices. It also detects automatically when OCPPHub itself is in its own demo mode (OHUB_IsDemoMode()) and then hides the controls for that device even when the tile's own demo mode is off.

✨ Details: clicking a device node opens its details as a separate, tile-filling page - with all contract fields of the device (e.g. voltage/current/cos φ per phase for meters, state of charge/plug status for wallboxes/vehicles), a power history with day navigation and energy bars for the last 14 days. Generated purely from the existing contracts - no additional configuration per device.

✨ Detail (enabling archiving by itself, 31.08.2026): if a device's power variable was not logged yet, the detail page enables archiving itself the first time the power chart is opened - instead of just reporting “no archive data”. The first call does not show any history yet; from then on the history builds up by itself.

✨ Detail (outlier protection, 01.09.2026): a single defective archive value from a partner module (found in practice: 261,554,185 W at night on a 9.18 kWp solar system) is now discarded instead of distorting the daily bar/power chart - a generic plausibility limit (1 MW), not a system-specific value.

✨ Detail (price contract for the federation, 31.08.2026): other modules can query the electricity price valid at any point in time directly from us via NRGDASH_GetPriceAt()/NRGDASH_GetPriceSeries() - real Tibber price slots where available, otherwise reconstructed from our own BDEW price history. A basis for cost evaluations over any period (day/month/year/lifetime), not just today - one price determination is enough for the whole federation.

✨ Details (node display, 28.08.2026): the battery node additionally shows the state of charge as a rising fill level; a red warning triangle appears directly at the affected node as soon as a diagnosis becomes conspicuous/critical; a dashed “ghost ring” compares the current power with yesterday at the same time of day; the solar node carries a progress ring (today's yield vs. daily forecast, if a PV forecast instance exists); the grid node shows an electricity price sparkline and switches every few seconds between watts and cost per hour (if a price source - Tibber Grid Rewards or automatically the BDEW household average - is available); the house chip carries a green self-sufficiency arc (share of today's consumption without grid import); the connection lines get thicker with power and show a small cross mark at the position of today's daily peak; with a StromGedacht instance installed, the grid traffic light tints the tile background subtly.

✨ Details (with many devices, 28.08.2026): from a larger number of consumer nodes on, the house node automatically switches from the circle to a “chip” shape (a pill with straight sides), so that the individual nodes do not have to keep shrinking despite many devices.

✨ Detail (display settings, 28.08.2026, extended by all remaining animation controls on 10.09.2026): whether inactive nodes are hidden or just greyed out, whether lightning arcs/glow are coupled to power and how strong these effects are, the active/inactive transition time, the flow speed (power for top speed of the running triangles), the automatic demo run and the animations on level change (3 variants each for success and blocked, plus “random”) are set by each user in the WebFront - pull the tile open with the double arrow (opens the instance's standard object view with the corresponding switches/sliders/selection lists) instead of searching for them here in the console. For example, a running automatic demo run can also be stopped directly in the WebFront.

✨ Detail (wallbox control, 30.08.2026): if a wallbox (ChargerHub or OCPPHub) is not controlled by any other instance (e.g. EMS/Tibber/§14a), the device detail page shows direct buttons for charging enable and current limit - independent of the manufacturer through the shared contract variable. For OCPP charge points, real charge start/stop commands and a one-time daily override ('fully charge anyway today') are added.

✨ Detail (current limit slider, 31.08.2026): upper/lower limits come exclusively from the respective device's contract (e.g. 5 A on some Tesla wallboxes instead of a flat 6 A) - never a hard-wired value. The slider also shows the percentage of the maximum charging power, a tick grid and marks half power as a point of its own, so that even with larger wallboxes (e.g. 32 A/22 kW) you can see immediately where you are on the scale.

✨ Detail (feedback on wallbox commands, 31.08.2026): every click on enable/limit/start/stop immediately shows a sending status. For start/stop, the wallbox's actual power is additionally reloaded after a short time - if it stays at 0 W after “Start charging”, a note appears that the wallbox has probably rejected the command. If the partner module supplies a concrete rejection reason through the optional contract field “blockReasonID”, it appears prominently right above the control buttons - independent of the manufacturer, no special case per vendor.

✨ Detail (start the tour yourself at any time, 01.09.2026): a clearly visible “?” button at the bottom left of the tile shows the introduction tour again at any time - regardless of the saved “already seen” status. Intended for shared instances (e.g. a demo/showcase instance with one shared login for all visitors).

✨ Detail (EMS reasoning, 03.09.2026): if the EMS module provides the contract EMS_GetCurrentDecision(), the tile shows a small field at the bottom with the current switching decision including a plain-text reason (e.g. “Grid charging – Grid Rewards (Tibber)”) - purely informational, the dashboard itself neither switches nor interprets anything.

✨ Detail (state of charge on a manual wallbox, 03.09.2026): a manually entered wallbox (“More consumers”) can additionally carry a “SocID” (directly in the saved list, not a form field of its own) - it then shows the state of charge at the node, as with automatically detected vehicles.

✨ Detail (isolated demo mode, 03.09.2026): the “Isolated demo mode” box (above, under “Demo mode”) switches off EVERY automatic device detection - grid/PV/battery/house then come exclusively from the manual core fields. Intended for a pure showcase instance with invented but internally consistent values - a mix of real live measurements and invented extra consumers would not add up otherwise. The electricity price sparkline at the grid node there (10.09.2026) also uses an existing real TibberGridReward instance first, like any other instance - only when neither Tibber nor the BDEW history provides enough slots (without Tibber at most one per day, too few for a visible curve) does the demo fall back to an hourly daily curve of its own, clearly marked as an approximation.

✨ Detail (wide tile used better, 03.09.2026): the arrangement now adapts to the actual tile width instead of always staying in a fixed square - with many devices (chip shape of the house node) considerably more of them fit side by side without having to get smaller.

✨ Detail (arbitrary extra values, 03.09.2026): a manually entered wallbox or other consumer can additionally carry any number of value fields of its own (JSON line, field name ends in “ID”/“IDs”, e.g. “vinID”) - they appear automatically in the “Current values” table of the detail page, exactly as with automatically detected devices.

✨ Detail (calmer lightning arcs on a wide pill, 03.09.2026): the lightning arcs on the house node now adapt amplitude and fineness to the aspect ratio of the pill - with many devices (wide, flat pill) they look fine instead of jittery, and are unchanged for a circular shape.

✨ Detail (drilling down, 03.09.2026, short/long assignment corrected on 09.09.2026): group nodes - virtual meters with sub-meters (MeterHubVirtual contract 1.3 “members”) or manual consumers with a nested “Members” - carry a meter badge. A short click/press always opens the detail page - as on every node and the center pill itself (also for members without a device of their own), with the familiar yellow time ring that fills up. Only a long press, during which the ring turns completely yellow, changes the level: on a group node it turns green, the node becomes the center pill and its members arrange themselves around it - with all functions of the first level, to any depth. Going back works the same way with a long press on the pill itself - a small “‹” badge at the top left of the pill edge (same look and edge position as the other badges - warning triangle/meter badge/minus badge) shows that a higher level exists, whose name is shown as a hover tooltip. An actual level change plays a small success animation (spark shower, portal iris - real overlapping blades around an off-center pivot in the same dark glossy metal look as the house/node coin, with a glass highlight in the middle, like a real camera aperture - head nod (the node nods around the horizontal axis) or drain (the node is sucked in like into a water drain); selectable behind the double arrow, including “random”). If it does not go in the respective direction (a leaf without members, or the pill on level 1), one of the four blocked animations plays instead (head shake - the real node/pill turns around the vertical axis -, circular waves - rings in the colour of the node edge travel outwards like a stone in a lake -, dizzy stars or little pile - the real node burns down from bottom to top, with a glowing edge, flames and smoke, and a little pile of ash remains briefly -, also selectable with “random”), without any effect. Long group names in the center pill itself stay inside the circle (only compressed, never stretched - when switching back, “House” appears in normal width again). Subtracted members (negative factor, e.g. “House consumption without wallboxes”) appear dashed with a minus - the hierarchy comes from the provider (MeterHub), the tile creates no groups of its own.

✨ Detail (09.09.2026): controls deliberately sit inside the tile's SVG content, not as an HTML element of their own at the tile edge - in the embedded view, the WebFront places its own native chrome over both the top (title bar) and the bottom edge of the tile, which hides or blocks any HTML overlay there, no matter which distance is chosen.

✨ Detail (09.09.2026): the automatic demo run occasionally also shows the health/diagnostics panel (solar yield vs. expectation, MPPT string comparison, insulation resistance) - in isolated demo mode without a real InverterHub instance, plausibly derived from the current solar value, so that interested parties also see this function in the demo.

✨ Detail (automatic demo run, 03.09.2026): the “Automatic demo run” box (above, default off) lets the tile open detail pages and nest/unnest group nodes by itself during inactivity - any touch pauses this for two minutes. Intended for showcase instances, so that interested parties see all views without having to click.

✨ Detail (switch groups, 03.09.2026): if MeterHubVirtual provides “switchID”/“switchStateID” (contract 1.4), the tile shows a small switch button at the node - grey/yellow/green for off/partially/on. A single member can be switched directly, a group switches all switchable (positive only) members at once - via the same transport-neutral RequestAction route as the wallbox control, so it also respects demo mode. Since 09.09.2026 also available on the detail page (long click) - before, only at the node itself, which is covered while the detail page is open.

✨ Detail (level 1 without double counting, 11.09.2026): if a consumer is a positive member of a group meter (e.g. “Light GF” and “Light UF” in “Light total”), only the group node appears on level 1 - the members can be reached by drilling down, instead of being counted a second time next to it. This also applies when the members still have their own dashboard assignment in MeterHub; MeterHub reports only each meter's own level, and the tile does the merging. Subtracted members (negative factor, e.g. wallboxes in a “House consumption without wallboxes”) deliberately remain nodes of their own - they are not included but calculated out. Which nodes were hidden and why is shown in the instance's debug window (channel “Nesting”).

✨ Detail (cost or revenue, 12.09.2026): the grid node switches every few seconds between power and money per hour - when importing as cost with a minus (“−1,04 €/h”, at the current electricity price from Tibber or the BDEW approximation), when feeding in as revenue with a plus (“+1,06 €/h”, at the feed-in tariff - automatically from the EMS, otherwise from the field below). Without a feed-in tariff entered, feed-in stays with the power display - feed-in is never again valued at the import price as apparent cost.

✨ Detail (feed-in revenue, 17.10.2026): the grid node's detail page additionally shows “Feed-in revenue today” and “Feed-in revenue this month” - fed-in kWh times feed-in tariff (form field below; without a tariff no row appears). The monthly total needs a real feed-in meter in the archive; it is calculated with the tariff entered today, negative spot-price quarter-hours (§ 51 EEG) are not deducted. In addition: annual and 12-month revenue, a recommended monthly advance payment and - with the form field “Monthly advance payment” - the reconciliation including a projection of the annual settlement (more paid out or to be refunded).

✨ Detail (cost per charging session, 13.09.2026): the detail page of every wallbox lists the charging sessions of the last 7 days with their actual costs - calculated per quarter-hour with the import price valid at that time (from the EMS, otherwise Tibber including past days, fixed price from the field below or BDEW approximation), only for the share that really came from the grid. Own electricity is shown separately beside it: solar power at 0 € plus lost feed-in tariff, battery power at its cost basis from the EMS (without EMS at 0 € and marked). Also works for a wallbox that is connected only via a meter.

✨ Detail (charging session at a glance, 05.10.2026): at the very top of every wallbox's detail page there is a simple overview of the current or last charging session - status, start of charging, end of charging, charging time, energy charged, cost and current charging power. By default the times are derived from the charging power (pauses of up to 30 minutes belong to the session); if ChargerHub (from contract 1.7, option “Plug times” in the data points panel) supplies the plug changes, “Connected at” and “Unplugged at” are shown there and - for CHARX/DaheimLader - the real charging time of the wallbox. Where the device offers a charging enable or current limit, there is a “Full power” button: it switches the charging enable on and sets the current limit to the maximum; you go back with the current limit slider.

✨ Detail (no current measurement, 13.09.2026): if a source reports the time of its last real measurement (e.g. ChargerHub/OCPPHub) and it is more than 5 minutes ago, the node shows “—” with “no current measurement” and a yellow warning sign - instead of presenting a frozen 0 W as “not running”.

✨ Detail (one grid node, one price, 11.09.2026): if several sources report a grid meter (e.g. a real-time meter and a billing meter that archives with a delay such as Inexogy), the energy flow shows exactly ONE grid node - the most real-time capable one. It carries the electricity price, center-pill balance, PV savings and house load estimate from one and the same selection; the other grid meters are attached to it as a fallback or secondary source and listed on its detail page as “Additional grid meter” (billing/delayed marked), but drive neither flow nor balance nor price. The hide list “Automatically found devices” remembers devices since this version by their power variable instead of by name - renaming at the source no longer makes a deselected device reappear; existing deselections are taken over automatically. Reasons in the debug window, channel “Grid meter”.

Automatic demo run: can now be set behind the double arrow in the WebFront (see the detail further below), no longer a console property.
Enable archiving of device power values

The charts on the detail pages need archived power variables. Only you switch the archive on: with this button for all found devices at once, or one by one in the archive instance. The tile itself never switches anything on.

Individual devices can be deselected here without re-entering them - e.g. if a device that was detected twice or is not wanted should not appear in the tile. Stays in place after the next “Search devices now” as long as source/role/name remain the same.

items.caption: Only needed if no NRG-Stack partner module (InverterHub, MeterHub, ChargerHub, HeishaMon) is installed or a value from there is missing. Complements the automatic search, does not replace it - both work at the same time. Below each field you see the current value with its sign and how the dashboard interprets it (updated after saving). If the direction is wrong, set the matching switch.

Any number of additional consumers, shown as circles of their own - regardless of whether they were detected through a hub module. Not every household has the same devices; the type determines the icon, the name the text below the circle (empty = default of the type). If the power variable delivers kilowatts instead of watts (e.g. some wallbox registers), choose kilowatt under “Unit” - the default watt corresponds to the previous behaviour. The last three columns only apply to the type “Wallbox” and may otherwise stay empty - they describe how the wallbox recognizes that a vehicle is plugged in.

Tesla vehicles via Tessie are detected automatically - only needed here for other makes without Tessie. With a wallbox plugged in, the vehicle that has just been plugged in is detected automatically (from the temporal proximity of the two “connected” reports) and its name and state of charge are shown at the wallbox - no fixed wallbox-vehicle assignment needed, even with several wallboxes/vehicles.

Only active with exactly one installed InverterHub instance (otherwise the assignment would not be unambiguous). The MPPT string comparison runs automatically. For “Yield vs. forecast”, additionally enter irradiance + a PV forecast instance. For the insulation resistance note, additionally set a warning threshold - without a threshold the raw value is shown but not rated.

items.caption: Tibber Grid Rewards instance for electricity price figures on the device detail pages (optional, otherwise automatic if there is exactly one instance)

items.name: FeedInTariffCt
items.caption: Feed-in tariff for the revenue display at the grid node - only needed without EMS, whose feed-in tariff automatically takes precedence (0 = no revenue display)

items.name: FeedInAbschlagEUR
items.caption: Monthly advance payment that the grid operator pays you for feed-in - for the reconciliation on the grid detail page (difference to the actual revenue, projection of the annual settlement); 0 = no reconciliation

items.name: PurchasePriceCt
items.caption: Fixed import price for the cost per charging session (gross) - only needed without EMS and with a fixed electricity tariff (with EMS the import price comes from there automatically); 0 = automatic (Tibber, otherwise BDEW household average as an approximation)

Own import price (gross, ct/kWh) with a valid-from date: if you have a fixed price or a tariff that differs from the BDEW average, enter it here. When the price changes, add a new row with the date from which the new price applies, so that past periods keep their old price. Takes precedence over EMS, Tibber and BDEW; empty = previous behaviour. A single energy price is assumed (no day/night tariff).

items.name: PurchasePriceList
items.caption: Own import price

Without a Tibber Grid Rewards instance, the nationwide BDEW household electricity price automatically applies as a rough guide (retrieved by itself from bdew.de every quarter, no further setup needed) - only with neither source at all are the cost/electricity price figures on the detail pages missing.

The circle colours are firmly tied to the respective quantity (solar = yellow, grid = green/red depending on direction, house = green-red gradient depending on the share of grid import, battery = blue) and cannot be changed.

items.name: ColorBackground
items.caption: Background colour (-1 = system default)

items.name: FontFamily
items.caption: Font (empty/“system” = system font)

All controls for the animation (hide inactive nodes, coupling of lightning/glow to power, effect intensity, active/inactive transition time, flow speed, automatic demo run) are set by each user in the WebFront themselves — pull the tile open with the double arrow instead of searching for them here in the console.
